# Payment status values

> The six states a payment record can be in: `PENDING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `REFUNDED`, or `UNKNOWN` (when the provider call timed out).

_Part of [Payment records and DTO service](payment-records.md)_

Every payment in the system lives in the `Payment` database model and moves through states as it is charged and paid. The `PaymentStatus` enum defines these states. When a payment is created, it's `PENDING`. As the system charges through Stripe, it becomes `COMPLETED` (charged), `FAILED` (refused), `CANCELLED` (stopped), `REFUNDED` (charged then refunded), or `UNKNOWN` (Stripe call timed out). When `UNKNOWN`, [the system queries Stripe later](resolving-unknown-payments.md) to settle it to `COMPLETED` or `FAILED`.

**Look at:** [`PaymentStatus` in payment.model.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/models/payment.model.ts#L33)

## Pieces

- [UNKNOWN status: provider call timed out](unknown-status.md): The charge may or may not exist; you don't know because the provider (Stripe) call timed out, not because the charge is still processing.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Payment.status` | ENUM column on the Payment table holding one of six status values per payment record |

## Watch out

- UNKNOWN means the Stripe call timed out—the charge succeeded or failed, but you don't know which. It's not a processing state you wait out.
- If a payment is UNKNOWN, never re-send the charge. Query Stripe first to see if it went through.
- CANCELLED happens before charging (buyer or system stops the request). FAILED happens after (Stripe refused the charge).
- REFUNDED payments were already COMPLETED first—this is not a first-time failure state.
